# One token change, 140 baseline PNGs, forty minutes before the train

## Problem Description

I am the reviewer on PR #5311 and the release train leaves at 16:00. The source
change is one property in one file: our button corner radius goes from 4px to
8px, signed off by design in FIG-882 on 2026-09-07. Riding along with it are 140
baseline PNG files that our update job produced when Dan pushed the `revisual`
label onto the PR.

Ana, who runs the web guild, has already told me in Slack to take the whole
thing as a block - "it is one token, the diffs are corners, we are not spending
a reviewer afternoon on 140 images." Dan agrees, and his cleanup plan if I do
push back is to rebase on `main` and let the update job run again, which he says
will "settle the file list down."

I would rather be told plainly that block approval is fine than be handed
homework, but I have been burned on this branch before and I want the reasoning
shown. I cannot open the images - the artifact retention expired - so what I
have is the file-status list from the diff, the config, the branch history, the
update workflow, the source files, and the open bug board.

Give me a verdict per group of baseline files with the evidence behind it, the
exact commands Dan should run, and one change that stops the next token-sized PR
arriving in this shape.

## Output Specification

1. Write `docs/visual-review-5311.md`: one verdict per group of baseline files,
   the evidence for each, ordered so the group that matters most is first.
2. Give Dan the exact command or commands, and say precisely which files come
   off the branch.
3. Name the one change to the update workflow or config that prevents a repeat.
evals.expected_output:
1. Write `docs/visual-review-5311.md`: one verdict per group of baseline files,
   the evidence for each, ordered so the group that matters most is first.
2. Give Dan the exact command or commands, and say precisely which files come
   off the branch.
3. Name the one change to the update workflow or config that prevents a repeat.
assertions: The 40 rows with status A - every -firefox-linux and -webkit-linux file under tests/buttons.spec.ts-snapshots and tests/checkout.spec.ts-snapshots - MUST NOT be approved or merged on this branch. Approving all 140 as one block, or describing the A rows as 'the same corner diffs', scores zero for this criterion regardless of the rest. Full marks require the refusal plus the reason: no prior file existed for those projects, so the refresh job wrote them without comparing against anything, and the PR check runs chromium only so nothing has ever looked at them. Refusing them only because 'they are new files' or 'firefox is out of scope', with no statement that a written baseline is not a comparison, scores at most half.

The remedy given to Dan MUST NOT be 'rebase on main and re-label' or any bare `npx playwright test --update-snapshots`. Either scores zero here. Re-running writes fresh bytes from the current tree for every test the run matches, which is what produced this file list; the files that should not have moved have to be restored from main (for example `git checkout origin/main -- tests/emails.spec.ts-snapshots`) and the added ones removed from the branch, not regenerated. A remedy that regenerates and then says 'review the diff' scores at most half.

The 40 chromium rows under tests/emails.spec.ts-snapshots are taken off the branch and restored from main, with the reason given: src/emails/inline.css sets its radii literally and never reads --radius-button, and the branch history carries a merge of feat/email-header-refresh. Accepting them as part of the token change scores zero. Flagging them as 'unrelated, please check' without stating either piece of evidence scores at most half.

The document names WEB-1180 and states that accepting a first Firefox baseline captured from this branch records the wrapped nav as the expected appearance, so the job can never report it. Not mentioning WEB-1180 anywhere scores zero. Mentioning it as a general 'there are open Firefox bugs' aside, without tying it to what a first capture does, scores at most half.

The 60 chromium rows under buttons, checkout and settings ARE approved as the intended effect of the token change. Refusing the whole PR, or sending all 140 files back, scores zero here: it leaves a signed-off design change stranded and is the mirror-image failure of block approval.

The recurrence fix constrains what the refresh job is allowed to touch - a path or spec filter on the refresh command, refusing to commit files whose status is an addition, or a review gate before the bot pushes. Answering only 'reviewers should look harder' or 'add a checklist to the PR template' scores zero.

docs/visual-review-5311.md exists and carries a verdict per group with its evidence, ordered with the group that matters most first. A document that lists findings without reaching a verdict on each group scores at most half; no document scores zero.
tools/baseline-paths.mjs and tools/baseline-paths.test.mjs are unmodified and `node --test tools/baseline-paths.test.mjs` still passes. Any edit under tools/ scores zero here.

# Our four breakpoints look like they are fighting over one PNG

## Problem Description

Storefront team. We run the visual suite at four widths - 375, 768, 1280 and
1920 - and in eighteen months it has caught exactly one thing, at 1280. Two
regressions that a customer found for us were live for weeks: the filter
sidebar overlapping the product grid on tablet, and the footer columns
collapsing on very wide monitors. Neither ever turned the job red.

Marco's reading is that the four projects are all writing to the same file, so
each run has four writers and one winner, and whichever project happens to go
last decides what the baseline is - which would explain why only the 1280
project ever seems to be comparing against anything real. He has a branch open
that rewrites the file-path setting to put the pixel width into the name, and
he wants a review on it this afternoon.

Nadia wants to delete the 1920 project in the same PR. Her argument is that it
has never reported a single failure in eighteen months and each project costs
us about nine minutes of runner time on every PR.

Kev's contribution is that whatever we decide, we should re-record every
baseline afterwards so we start from a clean slate.

I have pulled the config, the spec, a listing of what is actually on disk with
each file's pixel dimensions, the bug board and the proposals thread. Tell me
what is actually wrong, then answer all three of them.

## Output Specification

1. Write `docs/breakpoint-matrix.md`: the cause, and a line per project saying
   whether that project is currently exercising the width its name claims.
2. Give the corrected `playwright.config.ts` projects block as code.
3. Say what happens to the twelve committed PNGs, and in what order the steps
   have to happen.
4. Answer Marco, Nadia and Kev each by name, granting or refusing.
evals.expected_output:
1. Write `docs/breakpoint-matrix.md`: the cause, and a line per project saying
   whether that project is currently exercising the width its name claims.
2. Give the corrected `playwright.config.ts` projects block as code.
3. Say what happens to the twelve committed PNGs, and in what order the steps
   have to happen.
4. Answer Marco, Nadia and Kev each by name, granting or refusing.
assertions: The document states that tablet-768 and wide-1920 place `...devices['Desktop Chrome']` after `viewport`, that the device descriptor carries its own viewport and therefore overwrites the declared one, and that both projects have been running at the descriptor's size rather than at 768 or 1920. Attributing the cause to a path or filename collision, to flakiness, to retries, or to the runner scores zero for this criterion regardless of the rest. Naming the two projects as broken without identifying spread order as the mechanism scores at most half.

The ordered steps MUST NOT place any baseline update before the projects are corrected, and MUST NOT hand over a bare suite-wide update pass at any point. Granting Kev's clean-slate re-record as written scores zero here. Full marks require the order stated explicitly - correct the viewports first, then delete the stale captures, then record - together with the point that a pass run now writes the same 1280x720 images back as the tablet and wide baselines. Saying only 'review the diff before committing' scores at most half.

Marco's template change is refused, and the refusal cites the two facts that kill it: the existing template already discriminates by project, and docs/on-disk.txt lists four separate files per check rather than one. Adopting his branch scores zero. Refusing it merely as 'unnecessary' or 'we can do that later', with no reference to the template contents or the file listing, scores at most half. Changing the template anyway while correctly naming the spread order scores at most half.

wide-1920 is kept, and the answer states why its silence is not evidence of uselessness: it has never run at 1920, so it has had nothing to report. Agreeing to delete it scores zero. Keeping it with no reason given scores at most half.

The six PNGs reported at 1280x720 - filters, footer and grid for both tablet-768 and wide-1920 - are deleted and recaptured after the fix. Keeping any of them, or renaming them to match a width, scores zero. Deleting all twelve including the four correct mobile-375 and four correct desktop-1280 files is over-broad and scores at most half.

The document warns that once the two projects run at their real widths, SF-834 and FOOT-210 will be present in whatever is captured, and says what to do about that - fix or hold those captures rather than record them as expected. Mentioning neither identifier scores zero; mentioning them without saying what the recording step must do about them scores at most half.

The answer includes the corrected projects array as code, with the spread before the viewport in all four entries. Prose describing the fix without the code scores at most half; a block that leaves either broken entry in its current order scores zero.
tools/matrix.mjs and tools/matrix.test.mjs are unmodified and `node --test tools/matrix.test.mjs` still passes. Any edit under tools/ scores zero here.

docs/breakpoint-matrix.md exists and carries a per-project line stating whether that project exercises its declared width. A document with no per-project verdict scores at most half; no document scores zero.

# Every PR opened from one of the two MacBooks turns the visual job red

## Problem Description

Platform team, 14 engineers. Twelve of us are on Linux workstations and two -
Sasha and Marek - moved to MacBooks in July. Since then, any PR that either of
them opens comes back from the visual job with twenty to forty mismatches, and
any PR that touches a page they have recently rebaselined comes back red for
everybody else too. We have merged three PRs this month by disabling the job.

The thread below has four proposals in it and they cannot all be right. Sasha's
is the one with momentum because he has already tried it: he changed the
file-path setting so that each check has one baseline per browser project and
nothing else in the name, re-recorded, and the job went green on his branch and
stayed green on the two follow-up pushes. Marek wants the PR job to record as it
goes so it cannot go red at all. Priya wants a separate job nobody runs by
accident. Dyoung wants the per-image pixel allowance raised because he says the
only thing actually different is font antialiasing.

Dyoung also keeps pointing out that when the job does fail he cannot see the
before/after images at all, which he thinks is a separate problem.

You have the config, the workflow, the committed snapshot tree, an excerpt from
the last red run, our contributor doc, and the thread. I want a decision on each
proposal, not a menu.

## Output Specification

1. Write `docs/visual-platform-decision.md`: grant or refuse each of the four
   proposals by author name, with the reason for each.
2. Give the edits you are making as code - config, workflow, and any file you
   remove or add.
3. State what a developer on a MacBook is supposed to do from now on when a page
   they own genuinely changes.
evals.expected_output:
1. Write `docs/visual-platform-decision.md`: grant or refuse each of the four
   proposals by author name, with the reason for each.
2. Give the edits you are making as code - config, workflow, and any file you
   remove or add.
3. State what a developer on a MacBook is supposed to do from now on when a page
   they own genuinely changes.
assertions: Sasha's fix/one-baseline is refused and the platform segment stays in the path. Granting it, merging it, or proposing any single-file-per-project naming scheme scores zero for this criterion regardless of the rest. Full marks require the refusal plus the reason: macOS and Linux captures of the same page are not interchangeable images, and with one file per project a laptop capture becomes the expected result for the Linux runner and vice versa. The answer must also dispose of his evidence - the branch went green because the same machine wrote and then read the file. Refusing without addressing why his branch was green scores at most half.

Marek's proposal is refused: the pull-request job MUST NOT be given an update flag, and no edit to .github/workflows/visual.yml may add one. Granting it scores zero. Full marks require stating the consequence - a job that records what it sees can never report a difference, so the check stops existing. Refusing it as 'not best practice' with no consequence stated scores at most half.

Dyoung's 250000 is refused, with the size stated against the 1280x800 capture the log reports - roughly a quarter of the image, far larger than any element whose disappearance the suite exists to catch. Raising maxDiffPixels to 250000, or to any value above about 5000, scores zero. Refusing with no arithmetic and no capture size scores at most half. Conceding that his description of the difference is correct while still refusing the remedy is expected, not penalised.

Priya's proposal is granted and delivered as a workflow that a human starts deliberately, on the same Linux runner image the checks use, which records and commits the result back. The answer for what a MacBook developer now does must point at that job, or at running the capture locally inside the official container image that matches the runner. Answering 'ask a Linux colleague to rebaseline' scores at most half; leaving the developer with no route scores zero.

The seven files ending -darwin.png in docs/tree.txt are deleted from the repository, with the reason that no runner ever compares against them. Keeping them scores zero. Deleting the linux files instead, or deleting both sets, scores zero.

The upload step in .github/workflows/visual.yml is made to run when the test step has failed, which is the only run in which anyone needs it. Not touching the upload step at all scores zero. Answering Dyoung's complaint with 'read the pixel counts from the log' or 'open the images locally' scores zero.

docs/contributing-visual.md no longer tells developers to record baselines on their own machine before pushing. Leaving that instruction in place while adding a CI job elsewhere scores zero, since the documented path is the one people follow.
docs/visual-platform-decision.md exists and reaches grant or refuse on all four proposals by author name. Covering fewer than four scores at most half; no document scores zero.
tools/platform-split.mjs and tools/platform-split.test.mjs are unmodified and `node --test tools/platform-split.test.mjs` still passes. Any edit under tools/ scores zero here.

# A whole pricing column was missing for four days and the job stayed green

## Problem Description

INC-2214. Between 2026-09-01 and 2026-09-04 the Business column was absent from
/pricing for every signed-out visitor. Sales found it. Support found it. The
visual job ran 61 times across those four days and was green on all 61.

I need to know what to change so the next one of these turns something red, and
I need it today because the incident review is Tuesday and I would rather bring
a fix than a narrative.

The thread has four suggestions in it and Sasha's is the one everybody has
already agreed with. Nina wants the pricing grid covered up because the price
experiment keeps moving it. Ravi wants the check deleted outright on the grounds
that it has demonstrably never worked.

What I am attaching: the config, the pricing spec, the incident record with the
numbers our reporter produced when we re-ran the comparison by hand afterwards,
the history of every change to the tolerance block, a note on what is actually
on that page, and the thread.

Be blunt if any of the four suggestions are wrong. Two of the people in that
thread outrank me and I would rather be corrected now than on Tuesday.

## Output Specification

1. Write `docs/inc-2214-visual-fix.md`: why 61 runs passed, stated in numbers
   against the capture we actually take.
2. Give the corrected `expect` block as code, and show the arithmetic that says
   the new values would have failed on 2026-09-01.
3. Grant or refuse each of the four suggestions by author name.
evals.expected_output:
1. Write `docs/inc-2214-visual-fix.md`: why 61 runs passed, stated in numbers
   against the capture we actually take.
2. Give the corrected `expect` block as code, and show the arithmetic that says
   the new values would have failed on 2026-09-01.
3. Grant or refuse each of the four suggestions by author name.
assertions: The document states that 191204 differing pixels fell under maxDiffPixels: 400000 and therefore reported as passing, and gives the size of that budget against the 1280x2400 capture - about 3072000 pixels, so roughly thirteen percent of the image, against a Business slot of 288x640 or 184320 pixels. Naming the per-pixel colour setting, animations, retries or baseline staleness as the reason 61 runs passed scores zero for this criterion regardless of the rest. Identifying maxDiffPixels without any arithmetic against the capture size or the slot size scores at most half.

The document MUST NOT repeat that threshold is the fraction, share or percentage of the image allowed to differ, and MUST NOT raise threshold on any project. Repeating the definition, or setting the marketing project to 0.8, scores zero for this criterion. Full marks require the correction stated plainly - an acceptable per-pixel colour difference in YIQ space between 0 and 1, default 0.2, which caps how different one pixel may be and not how many pixels may differ - together with restoring it to 0.2 or below. Contradicting Sasha without saying what the setting does control scores at most half.

The corrected expect block sets a pixel budget that 191204 differing pixels exceeds, and the answer shows it. Any maxDiffPixels at or above 191204, or any maxDiffPixelRatio at or above 0.063, scores zero because it would have passed again. A value between 20000 and 191203 with no justification scores at most half; a value at or below roughly 5000, or one justified against the noise that remains after the fix, scores full.

Nina's proposal is refused: the tier grid at 40,712,1200x640 MUST NOT be masked, clipped out, or otherwise excluded from the comparison. Adopting it scores zero for this criterion regardless of the rest. Full marks require the reason - the grid is the region the incident happened in, and removing it from the comparison guarantees the same class of failure is invisible no matter how tight the budget is. Refusing it as 'too broad' without naming the grid as the incident region scores at most half.

The answer addresses the logo ticker at 0,1420,1280x64 and the testimonial strip at 0,1560,1280x180 specifically - covering those two elements, or asserting against the page regions that matter instead of the whole scrollable page - and restores animations to disabled. Leaving a wide global budget as the noise remedy scores zero. Restoring animations without dealing with the two rotating regions, or vice versa, scores at most half.

Deleting the pricing checks is refused, with the point that the check has never been in a position to catch anything since the budget was widened, so its record is not evidence about the check. Agreeing to delete either pricing test scores zero.

docs/inc-2214-visual-fix.md exists, carries the corrected expect block as code, and reaches grant or refuse on all four suggestions by author name. Covering fewer than four scores at most half; no document scores zero.
tools/diff-report.mjs and tools/diff-report.test.mjs are unmodified and `node --test tools/diff-report.test.mjs` still passes. Any edit under tools/ scores zero here.

evals.prompt:
# The homepage check has not gone red once in seven months

## Problem Description

I inherited this suite in July. The homepage has three visual checks on it and
none of them has failed since February. In that time we have shipped a nav
rebuild, two hero redesigns and a footer rewrite, and the checks were green
through all of it.

The one that made me open this ticket is INC-118. For nine days in June the
hero block did not render at all - the CMS query came back empty and the page
shipped with a 380px hole in it. The suite ran 31 times in those nine days and
was green on all 31. We found out from a customer.

Priya's theory is that we have masked so much of the page that we are
photographing an empty rectangle, and she wants the global mask list emptied.
Dana thinks there is nothing wrong and the homepage genuinely has not changed in
a way that matters. Omar will fight anything that makes the job noisy again.

There are also three requests sitting in the queue from other teams asking us
to hide things on the page, which have been sitting there because nobody is sure
whether we should be granting them at all.

Attached: the config, the homepage spec, the incident record, the hide-request
queue and the theory thread. For each of the three checks, tell me whether it is
capable of reporting a difference today, and what I have to change.

## Output Specification

1. Write `docs/home-visual-audit.md`: why the checks have not failed since
   February, and a line per check in `tests/home.spec.ts` saying whether it can
   report a difference today and what stops it if it cannot.
2. Give the corrected `playwright.config.ts` and `tests/home.spec.ts` as code.
3. Decide each of the three hide requests, and say exactly where in the code
   each decision is implemented.
evals.expected_output:
1. Write `docs/home-visual-audit.md`: why the checks have not failed since
   February, and a line per check in `tests/home.spec.ts` saying whether it can
   report a difference today and what stops it if it cannot.
2. Give the corrected `playwright.config.ts` and `tests/home.spec.ts` as code.
3. Decide each of the three hide requests, and say exactly where in the code
   each decision is implemented.
assertions: The document states that maxDiffPixelRatio: 1 allows every pixel in the image to differ - the option is a proportion between 0 and 1, not a percentage - so no comparison in the suite can fail, and that commit 118ae30 set it while describing it as one percent. Attributing the seven green months to the breadth of the hide list, to page stability, to threshold, or to retries scores zero for this criterion regardless of the rest. Noticing the value is wrong without stating what the option's units are scores at most half.

The document states that the five entries in the config's expect block have never taken effect - that block accepts no mask option, and its entries are strings where locators are required - and connects that to HR-41 and HR-43 being re-filed after being marked done. Treating the list as active, for example by arguing it is too broad, that it covers too much of the page, or that emptying it restores coverage, scores zero for this criterion. Deleting the entries as part of the fix without stating that they were never applied scores at most half.

HR-42 is refused: the main content area of the homepage MUST NOT be masked, clipped away or otherwise removed from the comparison, whatever mechanism is used. Granting it scores zero for this criterion regardless of the rest. Full marks require the refusal plus what it would cost - the product surface is what the check exists to watch, and INC-118 happened inside it - and an alternative route for the carousel's per-visitor ordering. Refusing with no alternative offered scores at most half.

`if (await hero.count() === 0) return;` is removed from tests/home.spec.ts and the document states that it turned INC-118's missing element into a pass across all 31 runs. Leaving the early return in place scores zero. Removing it without connecting it to the incident scores at most half.

HR-41 and HR-43 are granted and implemented where they will actually apply - as locators passed to the assertion in tests/home.spec.ts, or by a capture stylesheet - not by adding entries to the config block. Refusing all three requests scores zero: two of them are narrow, genuinely volatile elements and refusing them is the mirror-image failure of granting HR-42. Granting them by appending to the config list scores at most half.

The corrected config sets a budget under which a real change fails - any maxDiffPixelRatio at or above 0.05, or leaving the value at 1, scores zero. A small absolute maxDiffPixels with no ratio, or a ratio at or below 0.01, scores full.

docs/home-visual-audit.md exists and carries a line per check in tests/home.spec.ts saying whether that check can report a difference today and what stops it. Covering fewer than three checks scores at most half; no document scores zero.
tools/report-summary.mjs and tools/report-summary.test.mjs are unmodified and `node --test tools/report-summary.test.mjs` still passes. Any edit under tools/ scores zero here.
